# Configuration reference

Every setting, with its default, as in [`config/lorebase.example.yaml`](https://github.com/aantenore/lorebase/blob/main/config/lorebase.example.yaml). The services read one YAML file (`LOREBASE_CONFIG`), and an environment variable `LOREBASE__SECTION__KEY` overrides the key `section.key`; nested keys use more double underscores. Every key is optional.

```text
Lorebase example configuration.

Point LOREBASE_CONFIG at a copy of this file. Precedence, lowest to highest:
  code defaults < this file < environment variables LOREBASE__SECTION__KEY
(nested keys use more double underscores: LOREBASE__INFERENCE__LLM__BASE_URL).

The values below are the defaults compiled into the code; every key is optional.
Secret settings accept a literal, `secret://env/NAME` (environment variable) or
`secret://file//absolute/path` (file content).
```

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `logging.level` | `INFO` | CRITICAL \| ERROR \| WARNING \| INFO \| DEBUG |
| `logging.format` | `json` | json \| text |
| `logging.redact_keys` | `[password, secret, token, api_key, authorization, credential]` | field names whose values are masked in every log record |
| `logging.redact_min_length` | `4` | shorter secret values are not masked inside free text |

## `keeper`

Keeper, the REST API service. Environment: LOREBASE__KEEPER__PORT, LOREBASE__KEEPER__HOST, ...

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `keeper.host` | `127.0.0.1` | bind address; containers set 0.0.0.0 |
| `keeper.port` | `8080` |  |
| `keeper.api_prefix` | `/api/v1` | version prefix of every API route; OpenAPI at &lt;prefix&gt;/openapi.json |
| `keeper.request_id_header` | `X-Request-ID` | accepted from clients when well formed, echoed back |
| `keeper.problem_type_base` | `"urn:lorebase:problem:"` | error `type` URI = this prefix + error code |
| `keeper.trusted_proxies` | `[]` | networks of reverse proxies in front of Keeper, e.g. [10.0.0.0/8]. Only from these peers is X-Forwarded-For read (right to left, trusted hops skipped) to find the client address used by API key allowlists; empty: the socket peer is the client |

#### `keeper.limits.rate`

Token buckets per principal (API key id or user) and request class; refusals are 429 with Retry-After, every response of a limited route carries RateLimit-Limit/-Remaining/-Reset

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `keeper.limits.rate.enabled` | `true` |  |
| `keeper.limits.rate.backend` | `local` | local (alias memory): per process, N Keepers allow N times the limits; postgres: buckets shared by every Keeper (use it with more than one; compose scale-out and Helm with replicas &gt; 1) |
| `keeper.limits.rate.postgres` |  | the shared backend: UNLOGGED table rate_limit_buckets |
| `keeper.limits.rate.postgres.lease_tokens` | `10` | tokens taken per query and served from memory (at most a quarter of a bucket); unused ones expire, never overspent |
| `keeper.limits.rate.postgres.lease_ttl_s` | `2.0` | leased tokens not used in this time are dropped |
| `keeper.limits.rate.postgres.timeout_s` | `0.25` | budget of one query; slower counts as a failure |
| `keeper.limits.rate.postgres.on_error` | `local` | database down or slow: local (limits in this process), allow or deny; failed-authentication buckets always deny |
| `keeper.limits.rate.postgres.error_retry_after_s` | `1` | Retry-After of a refusal caused by the database |
| `keeper.limits.rate.postgres.check_cache_s` | `0.5` | reuse of a failed-authentication bucket reading by the check before each authentication (failures are written at once) |
| `keeper.limits.rate.postgres.auth_failures_timeout_s` | `1.0` | budget of a failed-authentication query; then 429 |
| `keeper.limits.rate.postgres.stale_reading_s` | `30.0` | during an outage a reading this recent still decides, so only clients without one are refused |
| `keeper.limits.rate.postgres.prune_interval_s` | `60.0` | deletion of rows of buckets that are full again |
| `keeper.limits.rate.postgres.prune_batch` | `1000` |  |
| `keeper.limits.rate.max_buckets` | `100000` | buckets kept in memory; least recently used are dropped |
| `keeper.limits.rate.exempt_paths` | `[/healthz, /readyz]` | route paths without the API prefix, never limited |
| `keeper.limits.rate.reads` |  | GETs, query, traverse, neighborhood |
| `keeper.limits.rate.reads.requests_per_minute` | `1200` | sustained rate |
| `keeper.limits.rate.reads.burst` | `200` | requests allowed back to back |
| `keeper.limits.rate.writes` |  | every other POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE |
| `keeper.limits.rate.writes.requests_per_minute` | `300` |  |
| `keeper.limits.rate.writes.burst` | `60` |  |
| `keeper.limits.rate.searches` |  | POST .../search |
| `keeper.limits.rate.searches.requests_per_minute` | `300` |  |
| `keeper.limits.rate.searches.burst` | `60` |  |
| `keeper.limits.rate.context` |  | POST .../context (context packs) |
| `keeper.limits.rate.context.requests_per_minute` | `120` |  |
| `keeper.limits.rate.context.burst` | `30` |  |
| `keeper.limits.rate.admin` |  | routes tagged `admin`: keys, principals, grants, audit |
| `keeper.limits.rate.admin.requests_per_minute` | `120` |  |
| `keeper.limits.rate.admin.burst` | `30` |  |
| `keeper.limits.rate.auth_failures` |  | 401s to requests carrying a credential, per client address |
| `keeper.limits.rate.auth_failures.requests_per_minute` | `30` | and per API key prefix; when either is spent, requests are |
| `keeper.limits.rate.auth_failures.burst` | `30` | answered 429 before the credential is checked |
| `keeper.limits.rate.auth_failures.ipv6_prefix_length` | `64` | IPv6 clients are counted by network of this length |
| `keeper.limits.rate.auth_failures.per_key_prefix_enabled` | `true` | false: count by address only (key prefixes are not secret, so with a bucket per prefix whoever knows one can keep that key throttled); the per-address bucket is always on |
| `keeper.limits.rate.domains` | `{}` | per-Domain buckets by Domain id, any of the classes above, e.g. supply: {writes: {requests_per_minute: 60, burst: 10}} |
| `keeper.limits.rate.routes` |  | how requests are sorted into classes |
| `keeper.limits.rate.routes.admin_tags` | `[admin]` |  |
| `keeper.limits.rate.routes.search_suffixes` | `[/search]` |  |
| `keeper.limits.rate.routes.context_suffixes` | `[/context]` |  |
| `keeper.limits.rate.routes.read_post_suffixes` | `[/query, /traverse, /neighborhood]` |  |
| `keeper.limits.rate.throttle_audit` |  | audit entry `rate_limit.throttled` for a principal that keeps |
| `keeper.limits.rate.throttle_audit.threshold` | `20` | being refused: this many refusals within window_s; 0 disables |
| `keeper.limits.rate.throttle_audit.window_s` | `300` |  |
| `keeper.limits.rate.throttle_audit.max_tracked` | `10000` |  |

#### `keeper.limits.quota`

Daily quotas per API key, in UTC days (users have none); exceeded: 429 `quota-exceeded` with Retry-After to the reset. Usage is stored in api_key_usage and shown by GET /auth/whoami

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `keeper.limits.quota.enabled` | `true` |  |
| `keeper.limits.quota.requests_per_day` | `100000` | null: unlimited |
| `keeper.limits.quota.context_tokens_per_day` | `2000000` | estimated tokens of context packs; null: unlimited |
| `keeper.limits.quota.flush_interval_s` | `5` | a process writes its counted use this often |
| `keeper.limits.quota.keys` | `{}` | per API key id, e.g. key_01...: {requests_per_day: null} |

In-process cache of GET read responses, keyed by Revision:

| `keeper.reads.cache.enabled` | `true` | commits move branches to new Revisions, so no invalidation |

| `keeper.reads.cache.time_travel_max_entries` | `128` | entries for reads at another Revision; 0 never caches them |

#### `keeper.auth.audit`

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `keeper.auth.audit.enabled` | `true` | hash-chained log of mutations and denied requests; needs the `database` section |
| `keeper.auth.audit.record_denied` | `true` | also record requests rejected with 401 or 403 |
| `keeper.auth.audit.write_timeout_s` | `2` | a failed or slow write is logged and counted, never surfaced |
| `keeper.auth.audit.reads` |  | records of successful reads, in audit_read_log (hash chains of their own), written in batches off the request path |
| `keeper.auth.audit.reads.enabled` | `false` |  |
| `keeper.auth.audit.reads.sample_rate` | `1.0` | share of the reads passing the filters that are recorded |
| `keeper.auth.audit.reads.principal_types` | `[]` | user, service, api_key; empty: every type |
| `keeper.auth.audit.reads.kinds` | `[]` | Kind api names in the route; empty: every read reads that showed or masked a sensitive value are always recorded, whatever the sampling and the filters |
| `keeper.auth.audit.reads.queue_size` | `10000` | past it records are dropped (lorebase.audit.reads.dropped) |
| `keeper.auth.audit.reads.batch_size` | `500` | records per transaction |
| `keeper.auth.audit.reads.flush_interval_s` | `1.0` | longest wait before queued records are written |
| `keeper.auth.audit.reads.write_timeout_s` | `5.0` | a failed batch is dropped and counted (on_overflow: drop) |
| `keeper.auth.audit.reads.on_overflow` | `drop` | drop: serve the read, drop and count the record; reject: 503 when the record finds no place in the queue, failed batches kept and retried (the read stream as proof) |
| `keeper.auth.audit.reads.retry_after_s` | `1` | Retry-After of reads refused by on_overflow: reject |
| `keeper.auth.audit.reads.unready_after_failures` | `3` | failed attempts in a row of a batch before readiness fails (on_overflow: reject) |

Thresholds and naming rules; a request may override them

### `keeper.agent_writes`

Operations that need review, written by agents (docs/agents.md) A request that names a `task` runs on the branch {branch_prefix}/{principal}/{task} and opens or updates a Proposal instead of answering 409 review-required. A Domain overrides any member with its own `agent_writes` setting.

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `keeper.agent_writes.enabled` | `true` | false: review-required stays a plain 409 |
| `keeper.agent_writes.principal_types` | `[service]` | principal types that are agents (user, service, api_key); the others must send auto_propose: true |
| `keeper.agent_writes.auto_propose` | `true` | default of agents when a request leaves auto_propose out |
| `keeper.agent_writes.auto_merge` | `false` | default when a request leaves auto_merge out |
| `keeper.agent_writes.allowed_roles_for_auto_merge` | `[]` | roles whose agents may be merged automatically (the role is granted in the Domain and covers the branch); empty: nobody. Required approvals are never skipped |
| `keeper.agent_writes.max_open_branches_per_principal` | `10` | task branches one principal may hold at a time |
| `keeper.agent_writes.branch_prefix` | `agent` | first part of task branch names |
| `keeper.agent_writes.branch_mode` | `overlay` | task branches: overlay (only the rows the task changes, reads the target as of the fork) or copy (full rows) |
| `keeper.agent_writes.delete_branch_on_merge` | `true` | delete the task branch when its Proposal merged or closed (not while another open Proposal uses it) |
| `keeper.agent_writes.max_task_length` | `60` | longest task slug (after normalization) |
| `keeper.agent_writes.title_template` | `"Agent {principal}: {task}"` | title of the Proposal |
| `keeper.agent_writes.summary_parameter_values` | `true` | list parameter values in the Proposal description; false: names only (values may be sensitive) |
| `keeper.agent_writes.summary_value_chars` | `80` | characters of a parameter value kept in the description |
| `keeper.agent_writes.max_summary_operations` | `20` | executions listed in one Proposal description |

## `inference`

Model inference, used by Scribe only. Lorebase never imports a model vendor library: every chat model is an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint, local or hosted.

### `inference.llm`

Tier 2; env aliases LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_MODEL, LLM_API_KEY

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `inference.llm.provider` | `openai_compatible` | openai_compatible \| fake |
| `inference.llm.base_url` | `http://localhost:11434/v1` | local Ollama; in docker compose: http://ollama:11434/v1 |
| `inference.llm.model` | `qwen2.5:7b-instruct` | any model name the endpoint serves |
| `inference.llm.api_key` | `null` | hosted endpoints: secret://env/LLM_API_KEY |
| `inference.llm.structured_output` | `json_schema` | json_schema \| json_mode. json_schema sends the schema as response_format and steps down (json_mode, then prompt only) when the server rejects it; answers are always validated |
| `inference.llm.json_schema_strict` | `null` | response_format.json_schema.strict; null leaves it out |
| `inference.llm.repair_attempts` | `1` | repair calls after an invalid answer (0-3) |
| `inference.llm.temperature` | `0` | null leaves it out, for models that refuse the parameter |
| `inference.llm.max_tokens` | `null` | completion cap; null leaves it to the server |
| `inference.llm.max_concurrency` | `2` |  |
| `inference.llm.timeout_s` | `120` |  |
| `inference.llm.trust_env` | `false` | false: proxy variables ignored; true: HTTP(S)_PROXY, NO_PROXY honored |

#### `inference.llm.retry`

429, 5xx and connection errors; Retry-After is honored

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `inference.llm.retry.max_retries` | `3` |  |
| `inference.llm.retry.backoff_base_s` | `0.5` | wait before retry n: min(backoff_max_s, base \* 2\*\*n), jittered |
| `inference.llm.retry.backoff_max_s` | `30` |  |

### `inference.llm` (continued)

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `inference.llm.price_per_million_tokens` | `{input: 0, output: 0}` | zero for local models |
| `inference.llm.headers` | `{}` | extra HTTP headers; values accept secret references |
| `inference.llm.extra_body` | `{}` | extra request fields, e.g. {reasoning_effort: none} |
| `inference.llm.tasks` | `{}` | per-task overrides, see the commented example below |

Example:

```yaml
# Hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Mistral, ...):
#   base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1
#   model: <model name>
#   api_key: secret://env/LLM_API_KEY
#   price_per_million_tokens: {input: <price>, output: <price>}
#
# Anthropic through its OpenAI-compatible endpoint (docs/inference-providers.md):
#   base_url: https://api.anthropic.com/v1/
#   model: claude-haiku-5-5
#   api_key: secret://env/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
#   headers: {anthropic-workspace-id: secret://env/ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID}  # org-level keys
#   temperature: null            # refused by current models
#   json_schema_strict: true     # required by the endpoint
#   extra_body: {thinking: {type: disabled}}
#   max_tokens: 4096
#
# LiteLLM proxy (compose profile `litellm`), reaching Anthropic, Google, Bedrock, ...:
#   base_url: http://litellm:4000/v1
#   model: <model alias defined in the proxy>
#   api_key: secret://env/LITELLM_KEY
#
# Small local model for bulk extraction, larger hosted model for schema discovery:
#   tasks:
#     extraction: {model: qwen2.5:7b-instruct}
#     schema_discovery:
#       base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1
#       model: <model name>
#       api_key: secret://env/HOSTED_KEY
```

| Setting | Default | Description |

| `inference.embeddings.cache_dir` | `null` | fastembed: where model files are stored (library default) |
| `inference.embeddings.threads` | `null` | fastembed: CPU threads (library default) |

```yaml
#   provider: openai_compatible
#   base_url: http://localhost:11434/v1

```

## `database`

Postgres 16 with the pgvector extension. Environment: LOREBASE__DATABASE__DSN, ...

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `database.dsn` | `postgresql+asyncpg://lorebase@localhost:5432/lorebase` |  |
| `database.pool_size` | `10` | alias LOREBASE_DB_DSN; e.g. secret://env/LOREBASE_DB_DSN. postgresql:// URLs are switched to the asyncpg driver; without a password, PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass is used connections kept open per process |
| `database.max_overflow` | `10` | extra connections under load |
| `database.pool_timeout_s` | `30` | wait for a free pooled connection |
| `database.pool_recycle_s` | `1800` | replace older connections; -1 never |
| `database.statement_timeout_ms` | `30000` | per statement; 0 disables |
| `database.migration_statement_timeout_ms` | `0` | while migrations run; 0 disables |
| `database.application_name` | `lorebase` | shown in pg_stat_activity |
| `database.maintenance_dsn` | `null` | optional secret: a role that owns mat_records, used by the job worker for per-Attribute index DDL queued by roles that do not own it. Alias LOREBASE_DB_MAINTENANCE_DSN. null: such roles skip index management (`python -m lorebase_store.indexes plan`) |
| `database.application_role` | `null` | role the services connect as; revisions 0005, 0008 and 0010 grant it EXECUTE on the security definer read functions (store schema notes); 0008 and 0010 refuse to run while it may CREATE in the schema of the tables or of pg_trgm. null grants nothing; the role must exist before migrating |
| `database.read_dsn` | `[]` | read replicas (docs/deployment.md): one URL, a comma-separated string or a list; literals or secret references, e.g. [secret://env/LOREBASE_DB_READ_DSN]. Alias LOREBASE_DB_READ_DSN. Reads are spread round-robin; empty keeps every read on the primary. Each replica gets its own pool, sized as above |
| `database.read_max_lag_ms` | `5000` | a replica lagging more than this serves no reads; 0: unchecked |
| `database.read_fallback_to_primary` | `true` | reads no replica can serve go to the primary; false: 503 |
| `database.read_probe_timeout_ms` | `2000` | budget to reach a replica and run its freshness probe |
| `database.prepared_statement_cache_size` | `500` | prepared statements per connection (asyncpg); 0 disables |

## `store`

Storage engine. `layout` and `embeddings` are read once by the initial migration; the other keys are read at runtime.

### `store.layout`

| Setting | Default | Description |

```yaml
# type_inference: options of schema inference (as keeper.schema_inference.options) that
# type new Attributes from their samples; defaults differ in min_support_values: 5,
# enum_min_values: 5 and propose_max_length: false
```

| `webhooks.connect_timeout_s` | `5.0` | connecting to one address; then the next checked one (&lt;= timeout_s) |
| `webhooks.max_attempts` | `8` | then the delivery is marked dead |
| `webhooks.backoff_base_s` | `30.0` | delay after the first failure ... |
| `webhooks.backoff_factor` | `2.0` | ... multiplied by this after each next one ... |
| `webhooks.backoff_max_s` | `3600.0` | ... up to this |
| `webhooks.lease_s` | `120.0` | a claimed delivery is retried by another worker after this; a pass running longer is abandoned (&gt; pass_timeout_s + timeout_s) |
| `webhooks.batch` | `100` | events and deliveries per worker pass |
| `webhooks.concurrency` | `8` | attempts of one pass in flight at the same time |
| `webhooks.pass_timeout_s` | `60.0` | no attempt starts after this; the rest go to the next pass |
| `webhooks.changed_keys_max` | `100` | changed Record keys listed per event payload |
| `webhooks.retention_s` | `604800.0` | finished deliveries kept (7 days; events: store.outbox) |

## `vault`

Personal data vault (design 13.5; docs/security.md): values of `pii` Attributes with `vault: true` are stored encrypted here, Records hold tokens, and `lorebase admin erase` erases them on every Revision. Keeper, Scribe and every committing process need the same keys.

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `vault.token_key` | `null` | secret://... (32+ characters) keying tokens and value fingerprints; never change it once values are stored |
| `vault.encryption_key` | `null` | secret://... (32+ characters) encrypting new values |
| `vault.key_id` | `"1"` | id stored with values sealed under encryption_key |
| `vault.previous_keys` | `{}` | earlier encryption keys by id, still opened |

## `scribe`

Scribe, the job worker (docs/scribe.md): Source synchronization, webhook delivery, queued per-Attribute index DDL (`store.index`, as database.maintenance_dsn when set) and garbage collection. Job retries and stale locks: store.jobs.

| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.streams` | `[actions, reads]` | audit_log and audit_read_log |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.signing_key` | `null` | Ed25519 PEM, e.g. secret://file//run/secrets/checkpoint.pem (openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519); verifiers need only the public key (openssl pkey -pubout) |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.key_id` | `main` | recorded in each checkpoint |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.prefix` | `lorebase-audit/` | object names: {prefix}{stream}/{UTC time}.json |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.sink` | `file` | file \| http \| s3 |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.directory` | `null` | file: a directory the database host cannot write |

#### `scribe.audit_checkpoints.http`

Http: PUT or POST of each checkpoint

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.http.url` | `null` | {name} is replaced by the object name |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.http.method` | `PUT` |  |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.http.headers` | `{}` | values may be secret references |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.http.allowed_schemes` | `[https]` |  |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.http.allow_private_targets` | `false` | off: global unicast addresses only, pinned, no redirects |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.http.timeout_s` | `10.0` |  |

#### `scribe.audit_checkpoints.s3`

S3: PUT signed with Signature Version 4; use a bucket with versioning or object lock and PutObject-only credentials

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.s3.endpoint` | `null` | e.g. https://s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.s3.bucket` | `null` |  |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.s3.region` | `us-east-1` |  |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.s3.path_style` | `true` | endpoint/bucket/key; false: bucket.endpoint/key |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.s3.access_key_id` | `null` | secret references, e.g. secret://env/CHECKPOINT_KEY_ID |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.s3.secret_access_key` | `null` |  |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.s3.session_token` | `null` |  |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.s3.allowed_schemes` | `[https]` |  |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.s3.allow_private_targets` | `false` |  |
| `scribe.audit_checkpoints.s3.timeout_s` | `10.0` |  |
